data.name: Guide_overview_Body
data.value: HappyMix helps your Discord server plan games, organize groups and events, and follow esports and game news. Sign in with Discord, choose a server, and use the tabs to manage your plans.

data.name: Guide_availability_Body
data.value: The calendar opens on today in the server time zone. Select a date to view its saved hours. Dots mark dates with separately configured availability. Enter your local start and end times, select a time zone, and choose definite or tentative. An earlier end time continues into the next day. Use All day for the full local day. Save to share your hours.

data.name: Guide_vacation_Body
data.value: Set a first date and optional last date to apply the same hours every day, including weekends. This adds dated availability alongside your weekly timetable. Overlaps prevent the whole save. Use the calendar to inspect dates and remove individual ranges.

data.name: Guide_weekly_Body
data.value: Open Weekly timetable and edit a weekday. Add one or more time ranges, set certainty for each, then save the day. The schedule repeats weekly. Copy day includes hours, certainty and time zone. Paste the copied text into another day’s editor, apply it, then save that day. Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V work in the copy field.

data.name: Guide_groups_Body
data.value: Create a group, add its description and games, and invite server members. Inside a group, the tab row at the top switches between Overview, Availability, Members, Events, Votes, Watchlist, Games and Settings. Invitees accept in Discord or the dashboard to join and receive the group role. The group board shows members’ availability. An open group is listed for everyone under “Open to join”: people ask to join and the organizer lets them in. Members can suggest games, found on any platform, for the organizer to add. Organizers and moderators manage the group. Role repair restores roles from saved membership. Leaving removes your group role. Closing a group deletes its membership records and role.

data.name: Guide_events_Body
data.value: Create an event for a group or choose individual members. Set its dates, hours and time zone. For a recurring event, accept once to join the series; decline or withdraw from individual dates without changing the others. The organizer confirms each date when enough people can attend, and can cancel one date or the remaining series. Confirmed events appear in availability. Open Channel notifications on a group or event to choose or create a channel named after it, set the language and reminder lead time, and optionally post updates when events are scheduled, confirmed or canceled. Events use their group’s settings until they get their own. Reminders mention accepted participants and the organizer only when they are absent from every server voice channel, including linked accounts. A repeating event sends each person one invitation: Accept all dates or Decline all dates answers the whole series. Canceled events and dates are erased a few minutes after cancellation.

data.name: Guide_game-news_Body
data.value: Create a subscription using a Steam App ID or store link and game name. HappyMix creates a channel and notification role. Members can join existing subscriptions or unsubscribe to remove their role. Creators and administrators can delete a subscription, its channel and role. Steam news is checked every ten minutes. Release, update and playtest headings are inferred from announcements. Member portraits require access to the Discord member list. Each subscription chooses what to post: patch notes, other announcements from the game's Steam page, and press articles. New subscriptions post patch notes and announcements; the creator or an administrator can change this on the game's card. New channels are created under Bot Notifications.

data.name: Guide_links_Body
data.value: Create a linking request from your primary account and open the approval link while signed in as the alternate. Both accounts must belong to the server. Review schedule conflicts before approving. Linked accounts share group membership and availability. Discord permissions remain attached to each account. Review the unlink preview before separating accounts. Administrators can manage links from their account tools.

data.name: Guide_settings_Body
data.value: Administrators configure announcement channels, time zone, reminders and notification types. “Where match posts go” shows which channel each game posts to and in which language, and warns when a channel mixes languages or is named for the other game; one click gives that game its own channel. CS2 and Dota 2 each have their own notification language, followed teams, Twitch channels and ping role; a new server starts with Ukrainian. Optional stream discovery links other live broadcasts naming both teams. By default it prefers Ukrainian-language streams and Ukrainian country and community tags; switch to custom lists to change them. Tick and order the ranking criteria. Country tags are self-declared, not verified location. Twitch credentials are required. Newly created channels use Bot Notifications.

Search the catalogs or paste a Steam, IMDb, TVmaze, MyAnimeList or AniList link: options then show the poster, year, genres, rating and seasons or episodes. Group votes are posted in the group’s notification channel; server votes in the channel you pick, or start one with /vote create. The dashboard shows who voted for what and today’s and this week’s results. Groups watching series, films or anime keep a Watchlist: add titles by search or link, mark episodes watched, note where you stopped (like 23:40), finish a series in one click, and add vote winners from the results.

While do-not-disturb is on, HappyMix holds your personal messages: event invitations and updates, group requests and invitations, and Live notices. data.name: Guide_stats_Body
data.value: Groups that play Dota 2 or CS2 have a Stats tab with a card for each member. Sharing is off until you turn on “Show my game stats to my groups”; it then applies to all your groups, and turning it off deletes the saved stats and matches. Dota 2 cards come from OpenDota (medal, wins and losses in the last 30 days, most played heroes) and need “Expose Public Match Data” on in Dota 2. CS2 cards come from FACEIT (level, Elo, K/D, headshots, maps) when the bot has a FACEIT key. When two or more sharing members play the same match, it appears under Recent games together, and the organizer can also have these recaps posted in the group's channel. Cards refresh every few hours and matches about every half hour, with links to OpenDota, Dotabuff, FACEIT, Leetify and Steam.
